target_customer: Digital health companies and direct primary care practices that need a programmable EMR
problem: Legacy EMRs are rigid and burden clinicians with admin work; digital health and direct primary care operators need an automation-first, API-driven record system.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per practice with tiers (Essentials 300 USD per month, Premium 550 USD per month, custom Developer tier)
product_category: Electronic medical record and health infrastructure

founders.name: Sharud Agarwal
founders.background_notes: Search results citing the company about page say he was diagnosed with leukemia in 2015 and started Akute after concluding healthcare processes needed improvement. The about page itself returned 404 when fetched, and the YC page founders section is empty, so education and prior employers are unknown.

technical_complexity.rationale: An EMR needs clinical workflows, e-prescribing, lab and pharmacy integrations and compliance, which is standard but broad engineering for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Medical records create switching costs once practices adopt it, but a four person team with a thin integration set faces many established EMRs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying Akute. These rivals are named only on later vendor comparison pages.

market_need_then: Growth of telehealth and direct primary care in 2020 to 2021 created demand for EMRs tailored to digital health operators. The company's own materials cite customers such as direct care practices. No dated quantitative evidence found.

branding.domain_note: Uses akutehealth.com (health suffix). Acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product marketing focused on automation and customization

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself, no mascot or community found. The name resembles the word acute, which fits healthcare but is easy to misspell.

outcome_analysis: Akute Health is still active with about four to five people and a product aimed at digital health and direct primary care operators. Revenue claims on aggregators suggest it may be largely bootstrapped, and no outside round beyond the YC deal could be verified. The story is therefore a small, slow growth software business rather than a venture scale outcome so far, but sources are thin.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: CB Insights shows 180K USD total, Elion 950K, Persana 960K over 2 rounds with a 2021-11 seed, Clera 1.5M, VCBacked a 2023-01 seed, and Latka says no venture capital raised. None is confirmed by a primary source so no round is recorded. Competition: Elation, Healthie and Canvas Medical appear on 2026 comparison pages but no source dated near the 2021 batch was found, so the list is empty. Founder section on the YC page is empty. Outcome search returned only unrelated news.
